description: UK National Curriculum 2014 lesson structure definition. Each component describes a phase of the lesson.

components.label: WALT
components.description: The main learning intention for the lesson, derived directly from the curriculum objective.

components.label: WILF
components.description: Success criteria that describe what a learner needs to demonstrate. Supports mastery learning.

components.label: Key Vocabulary
components.description: Subject-specific vocabulary learners must understand and use accurately during this lesson.

components.label: Starter
components.description: A short retrieval or warm-up activity (5–10 minutes) that activates prior knowledge and prepares learners for the new content.

components.label: Main Teaching
components.description: Direct instruction, modelling, and explanation of new concepts. Teacher-led, with opportunities for questioning.

components.label: Guided Practice
components.description: Learners practise with teacher support. Includes worked examples, think-pair-share, and mini-whiteboard activities.

components.label: Independent Practice
components.description: Learners apply their understanding independently. Differentiated tasks for developing, expected, and mastery levels.

differentiation.developing: Scaffolded tasks with prompts and sentence frames
differentiation.expected: Standard tasks meeting the curriculum objective
differentiation.mastery: Greater depth and reasoning tasks — applying knowledge in unfamiliar contexts

components.label: Mastery Check
components.description: A short, focused assessment activity (2–3 questions) that determines whether each learner has met the WALT. Results inform next lesson planning.

components.label: Plenary
components.description: Whole-class consolidation. Review WALT, share key findings, address misconceptions, and link to future learning.

SEN: Provide sentence frames and word mats
Use visual representations and concrete manipulatives
Pair with a supportive talk partner
EAL: Provide worked examples with step-by-step annotations
Accept home language as a thinking tool
giftedAndTalented: Apply concepts to real-world or unfamiliar contexts
Create their own problems or examples
